title: Sell Mineral Rights in Bridgeport, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Bridgeport, WV | Harrison County
metaDescription: Bridgeport, WV has grown fast, but old Harrison County mineral tracts underneath it still carry heir shares and flat-rate leases. We buy them directly.
heroLead: Bridgeport has grown faster than almost anywhere else in Harrison County over the past two decades, and a lot of that new commercial and residential ground sits over mineral tracts that were leased and subdivided in the wrong order.
intro: When farmland near the airport and interstate corridor got developed, mineral rights were frequently reserved by the selling family rather than conveyed with the surface, which means today's Bridgeport property owners often have no mineral interest at all, while the actual owners are heirs scattered well outside the county.

We buy oil and gas mineral and royalty interests tied to Bridgeport-area tracts directly, tracing the original farm parcel through the development that came after it rather than relying on current property lines.

sections.heading: Development outpaced the mineral record
paragraphs: Bridgeport's growth around the airport, the interstate interchange, and the retail corridor means a lot of the underlying mineral tracts were platted for commercial use long after the oil and gas rights were already severed and, in many cases, already leased. The current surface owner and the mineral owner are frequently unrelated parties.

sections.heading: Active leasing pressure in a growth corridor
paragraphs: Harrison County has seen sustained Marcellus and Utica leasing activity, and Bridgeport's position along the growth corridor means operators have had reason to pursue units here even as surface development continued around them.

sections.heading: Confirming your interest survived the development
paragraphs: Before we make an offer, we check the recorded severance deed and any later development plats to confirm your mineral interest is intact and identify its current lease or unit status.

faqs.question: I own property in Bridgeport but don't think I have mineral rights. Why?
faqs.answer: Many tracts near Bridgeport had oil and gas rights reserved by the seller before the surface was developed, so the current surface owner and the mineral owner are often different people.

faqs.question: My family kept the minerals when we sold land near the airport. Are they still ours?
faqs.answer: Likely yes, provided the reservation was properly recorded. We verify the severance deed as part of our review.

faqs.question: Is Bridgeport still seeing active gas leasing?
faqs.answer: Leasing activity varies by tract and depends on unit development nearby. We check current status before making an offer.

faqs.question: What if I only have an old handwritten deed for the mineral reservation?
faqs.answer: We can still work from it. We cross-reference older instruments against the official Harrison County deed books to confirm the reservation is properly recorded.
